definitions.explanation: A person who oversleeps or has difficulty waking up. Used affectionately or teasingly, especially toward children or close friends.

examples.japanese: この{寝坊助|ねぼうすけ}、{早|はや}く{起|お}きなさい！
{弟|おとうと}は{寝坊助|ねぼうすけ}で、{毎朝|まいあさ}{母|はは}に{起|お}こされている。
examples.english: My little brother is a sleepyhead and gets woken up by our mother every morning.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}は{寝坊助|ねぼうすけ}だったが、{社会人|しゃかいじん}になってからは{自然|しぜん}と{早起|はやお}きになった。
examples.english: I was a sleepyhead as a child, but I naturally became an early riser after I started working.

notes:
Compound of {寝坊|ねぼう} (oversleeping) + すけ (a suffix used to characterize a person, often with a playful or teasing tone). The すけ suffix appears in other character-describing words like {甘|あま}えんぼうすけ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {寝坊助|ねぼうすけ}を{起|お}こす: to wake up a sleepyhead
- この{寝坊助|ねぼうすけ}: you sleepyhead (affectionate scolding)

REGISTER:
Mostly informal and affectionate. Commonly used by parents addressing children or among close friends. Not used in formal or business contexts.

SIMILAR TERMS:
- {寝坊|ねぼう}: oversleeping (the act itself, not the person)
- {朝寝坊|あさねぼう}: sleeping in, morning oversleeping
